blurb: A reading map over Fanout's free AI research course — the roadmap, the glossary, the resource shelf, and three free sample lessons from the 108-lesson path.

adaptedFrom.name: Fanout (Suraj Gaud)
adaptedFrom.note: Fanout publishes no open licence on its site; Sikhi University has Fanout's written permission to build this reading map. No lesson text, video, lab code, or paper summary is reproduced here — every module is Sikhi University's own framing, and every card opens the real page at fanout.sh. The items below are Fanout's free public pages and sample lessons; the paid Pro curriculum (the remaining 105 of 108 lessons) is not included.

modules.title: Mapping the AI research path
modules.objective: Get oriented in Fanout's twelve-module, 108-lesson AI research roadmap before spending a single free lesson credit.
modules.teach: Fanout's path runs from math fundamentals through PyTorch, transformers, reinforcement learning, LLMs from scratch, fine-tuning, and MLOps. Start with the overview and the sequenced tracks, then keep the glossary and the foundational-papers reading order open in a second tab — most of what follows will assume you already know what the terms mean.

labs.title: Foundational AI Papers, in Reading Order

modules.title: Three free sample lessons
modules.objective: Work through Fanout's own free preview lessons — a research-paper writeup, an MLOps pipeline, and a modern architecture walkthrough — to judge the teaching before deciding whether the paid path is worth it.
modules.teach: These three are Fanout's own selected free lessons out of 108 — everything else in the course sits behind a paid Pro plan. They are a fair sample of the course's range: writing up a real experiment, building a reproducible ML pipeline, and reading a current research architecture.

labs.title: How do you turn an LLM experiment into a publishable AI research paper?
How do you build a reproducible ML pipeline with DVC and AWS S3?
How does a Tiny Recursive Model reuse one network to revise an answer?

modules.title: The resource shelf
modules.objective: Use Fanout's curated resource pages as a second opinion alongside the AI School's own AISF phases — courses, books, GPU guidance, and a hardware buying guide, organised by subfield.
modules.teach: Every page here is free and permanently public, not a lesson preview. Read them the way you would a well-kept bibliography: the deep-learning, machine-learning and reinforcement-learning resource pages each point at courses and books outside Fanout entirely, and the GPU and hardware pages answer the 'what do I actually buy or rent' question the phase content doesn't.

modules.title: Practice and community
modules.objective: Drill interview-style problems, find a study community, and keep an eye on where the research-engineering jobs actually are.
modules.teach: None of this is lesson content — it's the surrounding infrastructure a self-taught researcher usually has to assemble themselves: a tagged interview-question bank, hands-on challenges, an active-only community directory, and a jobs feed. Claude Code for Research is worth a look even if you never touch Fanout's paid tier — it's a free guide to using a coding agent for literature review and experiment iteration.

bench.title: Fanout Course Pricing
bench.note: The full 108-lesson path sits behind Fanout's paid Monthly, Quarterly, Annual, or limited Lifetime plans. Fanout also offers a verified student discount.
